My true preference is z > w > x > y. My priority at each school is w: 2, x: 1, y: 2, z: 1. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

I want to be matched to my most preferred school if possible. Since I have top priority at both x and z, I should propose to one of them first. Given that most people prefer y > x > w > z, it is less likely that z will be oversubscribed. Thus, I will propose to z first.

If I am rejected from z, I will propose to x. Since I have top priority at x, I will be accepted. I want to keep x as a safe option.

If I am rejected from both z and x, I will propose to w. Since I have priority 2 at w, I may or may not be accepted. It depends on whether the school is oversubscribed.

Finally, if I am rejected from z, x, and w, I will propose to y.

Therefore, my ranking should be z > x > w > y.

If I put z before y, I might get matched to z, which is even worse.

Therefore, submitting my true preferences should give me the best outcome.
